pr_title: Make a failure in ktls_sendfile a syscall error
pr_body:
a failure in ktls_sendfile results in an error in ERR_LIB_SSL, but its really a syscall error, since ktls_sendfile just maps to a call to the sendfile syscall.  Encode it as such

Fixes #23722
pr_comments: resolved discrepancy, please confirm everything looks good
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to the master branch. Thank you.

issue_context.title: SSL error differs for SSL_write()/SSL_sendfile() in broken pipe  scenario.
issue_context.body:
After upgrading from openssl1.0.x in the application implementing some HTTPS server, we attempted to  substitiute `SSL_write()` calls  in favour of `SSL_sendfile()` . Skipping the details the transition went smoothly, however, some discrepancy was noticed in the discrepancy in a few failure scenarios.
For instance, TCP connection drop by the peer scenario while doing write operation
  - for `SSL_write()` ends up with `SSL_get_error() ==  SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` and `errno == EPIPE`;
  - for `SSL_sendfile()` ends up with `SSL_get_error() == SSL_ERROR_SSL` and `errno == EPIPE`.

would it be better for `SSL_sendfile` to raise `SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` error instead, considering the fact they mostly come out s _sendfile()_ system call. It was confusing (to say the least) to see `error:0A000114:SSL routines::uninitialized` for the session, where previous writes were successful.
The error handing is quite poor here in [ssl_lib.c](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/openssl-3.2/ssl/ssl_lib.c#L2596), only `EAGAIN`/`EBUSY`/`EINTR` seem to be differentiated.
Please advise.

Definition of Done
```[tasklist]
### Tasks
- [x] Encode SSL_sendfile to raise SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL when epipe is returned from sendfile syscall
```
comments:
Can you test with this PR please:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/23723
I think it will fix the discrepancy
was the issue corrected with the patch?
@nhorman thanks for the quick response. the code changes seem to be promising. it will take a couple of days to verify it in practice. I'll get back to you once I am done.

There's also a breaking change between 3.1 and 3.2 with KTLS, nonblocking and SSL_write returning SSL_EROR_SSL and errno EAGAIN.
Version 3.1 didnt have this behaviour. It looks like it returned SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE directly.

Sidenote: The captcha for registering an account with github is insane. I dont want to spend 5 minutes clicking on dart-boards.

> was the issue corrected with the patch?

@nhorman 
the patch has been tested against EPIPE failure scenario.
Although the `SSL_get_error()` is  become `SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` with the patch applied, there is a tiny discrepancy remained.
 - for `SSL_write()`:  the error value retrieved via _ERR_peek_error()_ is equal to 0, and the system error is available in `errno` only. 
 - for `SSL_sendfile()`:  _ERR_peek_error()_ is non-zero (`0x80000020`), and  `ERR_GET_REASON(ERR_peek_error()) == errno` (EPIPE = 0x20)
 
 the question is  as follows: 
 in order to have a common error handling in the application what should be a reliable source  for error reason: `errno` or   `ERR_GET_REASON(...)`?
 Please advise.

I have just grep'd throughout the code and found that the pattern:
```c
ERR_raise_data(ERR_LIB_SYS, get_last_socket_error(),
      "calling some_socket_system_function()"); 
```
is widely used in `crypto/bio/*.c` files for the most of socket operations like _ioctl()_, _getsockopt()_, _accept()_, _connect()_ etc,  but never met when doing write/read. 
was it done intentionally or omitted?

Thats odd, I made no changes to SSL_write, but you noted in your initial post that an error on SSL_write SSL_get_error returns SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, which is retrieved based on a call to ERR_peek_error(), so its not making much sense to me that now its not returning an error at all ?

ok, thank you for the clarification, so in both cases ERR_peek_error on the SSL_write case, regardless of the patch status returns 0 for you.  That makes more sense.

Though, its still confusing.  SSL_get_error calls ossl_ssl_get_error to determine the error return code, and SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL is returned if and only if the following conditions are met:
1) the passed in check_err parameter is 1 (which it is)
2) ERR_peek_error does _not_ return zero
3) The ERR_GET_LIB  value of the value returned from ERR_peek_error is ERR_LIB_SYS

That suggests to me that the error stack is being cleared between the time you call SSL_get_error and the time you call ERR_peek_error.

do you happen to have a small reproducer I can use to try this here?

@nhorman 


> SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL is returned if and only if the following conditions are met:
> 
> 1. the passed in check_err parameter is 1 (which it is)
> 2. ERR_peek_error does _not_ return zero
> 3. The ERR_GET_LIB  value of the value returned from ERR_peek_error is ERR_LIB_SYS

it seems not to be a _true_ statement. there are other possibilities for `ossl_ssl_get_error ()` to return _SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL_. What I believe is happening when `SSL_write()` encounters EPIPE error,  `ERR_raise_data()` is not invoked,  `ERR_peek_error()` thereby is zero, and `SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` comes out  from the very last return of this function: [`ssl_lib.c:4703`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/openssl-3.2.1/ssl/ssl_lib.c#L4703).

As I mentioned when handling negative retvalue during write socket operation, only check against _non-fatal_ errno values is made, and no error raised
Please refer to [`int sock_write(BIO *b, const char *in, int inl)`](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/openssl-3.2.1/crypto/bio/bss_sock.c#L169)  implementation.

And you may compare how socket `connect()` returning -1 is handled [here](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/openssl-3.2.1/crypto/bio/bio_sock2.c#L153). (i.e. the error is raised unless `errno` is _non-fatal_, _retriable_.)
thank you, I see whats happening now.  Let me see what I can do here
updated the PR to take care of this

review_comments: Hmm. The code above uses `get_last_sys_error`, but this uses `get_last_socket_error` which looks strange.

If I understand difference between `GetLastError()` (`get_last_sys_error()`) and `WSAGetLastError()` (`get_last_socket_error()`) right, then we really should be using `get_last_socket_error()` here so we can obtain error code from socket subsystem on windows. The lines above should be changed as well, I think. Perhaps it should be done in seperate PR.

The `get_last_sys_error()` vs. `get_last_socket_error()` only matters on windows. On other OSes both macros are alias of `errno`.
@Sashan is right, on linux it should be the same, since their both aliased to errno, but you're right @mattcaswell it should be get_last_sys_error for consistency
updated to use get_last_sys_error, and added a simmilar error for SSL_write
I am not sure this kind of changes should be done in stable releases. Especially the change for SSL_write().
you think it should be targeted for the next minor release?  Or is this a major-only change?
IMO OK for a minor release.
